title: Dashboards + alerts for Dedicated burst pool saturation/denials (with label cardinality constraints)
creator: Allison Grant
description:
Build the Grafana dashboard(s) + alert rules for burst capacity (Dedicated): burst pool saturation, admission/denial rates, denial reasons, queue depth/backpressure signals, and neighbor impact indicators. Include clear links to SRE runbooks + oncall annotations, and enforce label/cardinality constraints so we don’t DOS Prometheus/Grafana at GA.

This ticket covers:
- Final dashboard UX (panels + templating variables)
- Alert rules + routing + paging policy alignment
- Documentation in dashboard (panel descriptions) + runbook links
- Label cardinality constraints (what labels we allow, what labels are forbidden)

Not covered:
- Implementing the underlying metrics in services (tracked in ENG-4810 / PR-23822)
- Implementing SLO gate auto-disable (tracked in ENG-23988 / ENG-4902)

Artifacts / related:
- Confluence dashboard catalog: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/burst-capacity-dashboards.json
- SLO/alerting policy doc: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-burst-slos-and-alerting.json
- Overload runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/burst-pool-overload-mitigation-runbook.json
- Metrics taxonomy draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/burst-metrics-taxonomy.json
- Grafana/alerts PR (observability-pack): sources/github/observability-pack/pr-612-add-burst-pool-dashboards.json
acceptance_criteria:
1) Grafana dashboards exist in observability-pack and are deployed to staging + prod.
2) Dashboards include: burst saturation (pool-level), denials breakdown (reason code), per-tenant burst usage summary, and neighbor impact indicators.
3) All panels have descriptions with: what it means, expected ranges, and a runbook link.
4) Alert rules exist for: pool saturation, denial spikes (overall + reason-code specific), admission controller timeouts/errors, telemetry lag high, and global circuit breaker active.
5) Alerts are tuned to avoid noise (no page storms) and align with SRE paging policy; warning vs page separation.
6) Label cardinality constraints are documented and enforced (dashboards do not require high-cardinality labels; alerts do not group by tenant_id/request_id/model).
7) Runbook links are present and point to the correct Confluence runbooks.
8) SRE sign-off captured in ticket comments (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes).
implementation_notes:
Dashboards
- Folder: Dedicated > Burst Capacity
- Primary dashboard: “Burst Pools: Saturation + Denials”
  - Variables: region, hardware_class, pool_name (pool_name is bounded set from config; no free-form).
  - Panels:
    - Pool utilization (allocated_gpu / pool_capacity) + saturation gauge
    - Burst admitted vs denied (rate) with stacked breakdown
    - Queue depth / backpressure (if queue mode enabled) and time-in-queue p95
    - Denial reason codes (top-N) with table + sparkline
    - Admission controller latency/error rate (p50/p95 + 5xx rate)
    - Telemetry lag (seconds) and smoothing window
    - Global circuit breaker state (on/off) and ‘fleet safety cap exceeded’ counter
- Secondary dashboard: “Tenant Burst: Usage + Limits (Support view)”
  - Variables: tenant_slug (restricted to allowlisted tenants only in internal folder; do not expose as a global variable in customer-facing folder)
  - Panels:
    - Burst GPU-seconds / hour (or burst token-seconds) and % of configured cap
    - Denial reason breakdown for that tenant (bounded reason codes)
    - Time windows where cooldown active
    - Annotations: config changes / feature flag toggles (from audit events)

Alerts (Prometheus)
- Pool saturation
  - Warn: utilization > 0.80 for 10m
  - Page: utilization > 0.90 for 10m OR utilization > 0.95 for 3m
- Denial spike (protects customer experience + signals pool exhaustion)
  - Warn: denied_rate / request_rate > 0.15 for 10m (only when request_rate above floor)
  - Page: denied_rate / request_rate > 0.30 for 10m (same floor)
- Denial reason specific
  - Page only for: admission_controller_error, telemetry_stale, circuit_breaker_active (these indicate platform issue vs expected capacity)
- Admission controller health
  - Page: 5xx rate > 1% for 5m OR p95 latency > 250ms for 10m
- Telemetry lag
  - Warn: telemetry_lag_seconds p95 > 30s for 10m
  - Page: telemetry_lag_seconds p95 > 60s for 10m (ties to known beta failure mode)
- Circuit breaker
  - Page immediately: global_circuit_breaker_active == 1 for > 2m

Label/cardinality constraints
- Hard rules (do not use in dashboard queries, do not group alerts by): request_id, trace_id, prompt_hash, model_revision, user_id, endpoint_path, org_id.
- Allowed labels (bounded sets): region, hardware_class, pool_name, decision (admit/deny), reason_code (bounded enum), tier (gold/silver/standard), tenant_tier (bounded), route_class (bounded), result (ok/error).
- Tenant-level visibility
  - For internal-only dashboards, allow tenant_slug but do not emit tenant_id label on every metric; prefer metrics exported via dedicated ‘usage report’ pipeline or queryable logs.
  - If we must include tenant context for a small subset of metrics, cap to allowlisted tenants only and keep it behind a separate metric namespace with strict scrape limits.

Runbook links
- Overload mitigation runbook: “Burst pool overload mitigation” (Confluence)
- Support denial reason codes: link to ENG-4881 / docs section (once merged)
- Circuit breaker runbook section: include ‘disable burst globally’ instructions + feature-flag name

Notes on noise
- All ratio alerts must include a low-traffic guard: request_rate > X (per pool). Avoid paging on tiny denominators.
- Alerts should group by (region, hardware_class, pool_name) only.
- Prefer alert annotations pointing to the dashboard + runbook; avoid free-form long text.
